analysis.title: ITC Overnight News & Press with Links, 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: Israel election exit polls show Netanyahu's coalition tied with the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot at about 51 seats each in the 120-seat Knesset. Likud is projected to stay the largest party with 24-27 seats. Neither camp is near the 61 needed, so coalition talks are likely to run long.

Iran threatened South Korean shipping group Sinokor with legal action over alleged violations of its Strait of Hormuz transit rules (FT). This is the first known direct threat against a named shipowner.

WSJ reports the US has told Gulf Arab states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign against Iran after the US midterms. The aim is reportedly to degrade Iran's military and push it back to negotiations.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the US may let more Russian diesel reach global markets, depending on Russia's actions. The recent suspension of sanctions on Russian diesel exports is meant as an incentive toward ending the Ukraine war and should modestly ease fuel supply.
API reported US crude inventories fell 2.031M barrels in the week ending Oct 23, against analyst expectations. Gasoline rose 2.39M barrels and distillates rose 380K barrels.
Australia September CPI came in at +4.3% y/y vs +4.2% estimated, and +0.8% m/m vs +0.7% estimated. Q3 CPI was +1.3% q/q vs +1.2% estimated, and Q3 trimmed mean was +3.7% y/y vs +3.6% estimated.

RBA Governor Bullock said upside inflation risks are materializing and price pressures are likely to exceed the August projections. This strengthens the case for another rate increase at the next meeting.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand unexpectedly held the Official Cash Rate at 2.75% when most economists expected a hike. The New Zealand dollar fell. The RBNZ said further tightening may still be needed, depending on data.

SK Hynix Q3 revenue was 104.62 trillion won vs 98.34 trillion expected. Operating profit was 83.33 trillion won vs 76.72 trillion expected. It announced more than $25 billion in dividends and buybacks.
OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google's AI chips (The Information via Reuters), deepening ties between two competitors. OpenAI already offers its models through Google Cloud.

FT reports the US and Russia are discussing a return of US oil majors to Russian projects as part of Ukraine peace talks. Ideas include reviving Sakhalin ventures and Druzhba pipeline exports to Europe after a settlement.

The European Commission is pressing G7 nations for more Ukraine funding. Non-EU commitments may fall to about EUR 4B next year from EUR 19B in 2026, and the US, UK, Canada and Japan are expected to provide about EUR 1B together.
General Motors plans to move its listing from the NYSE to Nasdaq, citing its focus on autonomous vehicles and AI-powered manufacturing.

The UK Budget is expected to include removing gas standing charges (up to GBP 50 off annual bills), limits on new net-zero levies, an extended VAT cut on electricity, and winter support for lower-income households. Chancellor Healey is also expected to drop the cut to the Cash ISA allowance from GBP 20,000 to GBP 12,000.
The Netherlands plans to cut 25,000 civil service jobs (about 15%) over a decade through AI-driven efficiency, saving EUR 3.5B a year, with about EUR 900M in budget savings by next year.
